"""
Modi government tries to solve India's job math with new skill definition

The new definition will clearly outline what constitutes skills and the ministry hopes to see a substantial increase in the number of skilled personnel based on the new definition.

The skill development and entrepreneurship ministry is readying to release a definition of skills in line with international standards, two years after it launched the Skill India Mission.

The new definition will clearly outline what constitutes skills and the ministry hopes to see a substantial increase in the number of skilled personnel based on the new definition when the statistics and programme implementation ministry comes out with the next National Sample Survey Office survey on vocational training in 2020.

"We plan to come up with a clear definition of skills that is aligned with international standards and fulfils the purpose of getting data to give us the actual number of skilled personnel in the country," skill development and entrepreneurship secretary KP Krishnan told ET.

Only people trained for vocational education from Industrial Training Institutes under the erstwhile Skills Development Initiative are accounted for under the existing rules for measuring skills in the country. "As per the last survey, the numbers for vocational training are dismally low when compared to other countries. A lot of initiatives are being taken to impart quality skills training under this government and the idea of defining skills is to widen the base and capture the real picture," Krishnan said.

The NSSO survey on vocational training is done every five years and the next survey is due in 2020. "Many rounds of discussions have taken place between the ministries of skill development and entrepreneurship, and statistics and programme implementation," said a senior official in the statistics and programme implementation ministry. "User ministries put in their recommendations and an expert group takes a call on those. Then we see how possible it is to do data collection. However, they need to give us a definition of skills first."

The latest NSSO survey on vocational training, conducted in 2015, shows just 2.2% of those aged between 15 and 59 years received formal vocational training while 8.6% in the same age group received non-formal vocational training.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi had in 2015 launched the Skill India Mission, which has an ambitious target of imparting skills to about 40.2 crore workers by 2022. 'Good morning, Alex.'

'It would appear so. Are the others not here yet?'

'Nah. Wouldn't expect them to be, either. Jon's probably not up yet, Eddie's had to do his paper round and Tony's probably got caught up in another running battle with his sister.'

'Ah, right. Do you suppose they'll be long?'

'Shouldn't be. Except maybe for Jon. Likes his bed, does Jon.'

'Don't we all,' said Spike ruefully, 'don't we all?'

'Yeah, like you say, don't we all?'

They fell into an awkward silence. This was the first time he had been alone with their new friend, and now that he was, he didn't quite know what to say to him.

'Er...are you still up for all this?'

Spike shrugged. 'Why shouldn't I be? It's a good plan.'

'Yeah, but you ain't...you know...'

Spike didn't answer, just shrugged again as though to say that he didn't really need a reason to be involved, he just wanted to be. Al sneaked a sidelong look at his friend, seemed to be trying to understand something.

'Tell me,' he said, 'why are you hanging out with us guys?'

'At the risk of sounding flippant, I believe you invited me to.'

'Yeah but why? I mean, I'd have thought once you'd done your time at our school, you'd be wanting to be back with your own friends, come the weekend.'

'And so I might. It just so happens that I enjoy your company.' He paused, a little reflective. 'Being at a private school can be pretty constricting at times. One is expected to uphold certain standards of behaviour, follow certain rules and all that. It's really quite refreshing to be conducting oneself in a manner not befitting a student of Chapworthy College for a change.'

'Yeah? Is it really that bad?'

'You wouldn't know it.'

Al let go a low whistle. 'And I thought _we_ had it rough. Sounds like they regard you as college boy first and human being second.'

'I'd never thought of it in that way,' said Spike wistfully. 'But you know, you're right, you're absolutely right...'

Al looked up. 'They're here,' he said, and they were, wending their way through the throng towards them. 'You're late!' he yelled.

'Only by a few minutes,' Tony yelled back.

'That's still late. Did anyone bring any money?'

'Just a moment,' said Spike, 'I thought I was providing the finance for this little jaunt.'

'Sorry but we can't let you do that,' said Al. 'So we decided to scrounge what we could, pool it and see what we ended up with.'

'Oh? And when was this decided?'

'Last night. After you went home. We took a gang vote on it.

prompt: What is the proper way to use a cocktail shaker, and what are some tips for making excellent cocktails?
response:
The proper way to use a cocktail shaker is as follows:

1. Fill your shaker with ice, leaving enough room for the desired amount of liquor and any other ingredients.

2. Add the liquor and any other ingredients (such as juice, syrup, or bitters) into the shaker.

3. Securely fasten the lid onto the shaker and shake vigorously for approximately 15-20 seconds, depending on the recipe. The shaking motion aerates the mixture, which helps to create a smooth and frothy texture.

4. Strain the cocktail into a glass, either by pouring it through a fine mesh strainer or using a Hawthorne strainer.

Tips for making excellent cocktails include:

1. Use high-quality, fresh ingredients. Fresh citrus juices, herbs, and spices can make all the difference in the flavor of your cocktail.

2. Measure accurately. Cocktails are carefully balanced drinks, so it's important to measure out each ingredient precisely to ensure the correct ratio.

3. Chill your glasses beforehand. This will help to keep your cocktail colder for longer, making it more refreshing and enjoyable to drink.

4. Don't overshake. While shaking helps to aerate the mixture, too much shaking can result in a watery texture and dilute the flavors. Shake only until you see small ice crystals forming on the inside of the shaker.

5. Experiment with different garnishes. A well-placed garnish not only looks attractive but can also add an extra dimension of flavor to your cocktail.

6. Know when to stir instead of shake. Some cocktails, such as the classic Martini, are better made by stirring rather than shaking. Stirring helps to preserve the clarity and integrity of the spirit and prevents the drink from becoming too cold or diluted.

By following these tips and techniques, you'll be well on your way to creating delicious and impressive cocktails every time!

Tom Jans (February 9, 1948 – March 25, 1984) was an American folk singer-songwriter and guitarist from San Jose, California. He is perhaps best known for his song "Loving Arms" (also known as "Lovin' Arms"), which was recorded initially by Kris Kristofferson and Rita Coolidge, and later by artists including Dobie Gray, Elvis Presley, Dixie Chicks, Natalie Cole, Olivia Newton-John, Petula Clark, Jon English, Livingston Taylor, Etta James, Millie Jackson, Jody Miller, The Beautiful South, Irma Thomas and The Cats.

Early life 
The son of a farmer, Tom Jans was raised near San Jose. Jans's paternal grandmother had been involved in music, playing in the Rocky Mountain Five jazz group. His influences ranged from Hank Williams to flamenco (his mother was from Spain) to The Beatles. He studied English literature at the University of California at Davis, but rejected a graduate scholarship to Columbia University to seek a career in music.

Career 
Playing coffeehouses in San Francisco, Jans met Joan Baez, who introduced him to her sister Mimi Fariña in 1970. Fariña had achieved cult status as part of a duo with her late husband Richard Fariña. Fariña had begun writing new songs and was looking for a partner to perform them with; Jans seemed to be a similar collaborator and the two formed a new duo. The duo played San Francisco Bay Area clubs and received notice from their performance at the Big Sur Folk Festival. The group then toured extensively as a supporting act for Cat Stevens and then James Taylor. They received a recording contract from A&M Records, releasing the album Take Heart in 1971. However, the album received little notice and the duo split up in 1972.

Jans moved to Nashville to pursue work as a songwriter, working for the publishing house Irving/Almo. His first hit as a writer was the song "Loving Arms", initially recorded by Kris Kristofferson and Rita Coolidge and then by Dobie Gray and Elvis Presley in 1973. Jans put the song on his self-titled solo debut album on A&M Records in 1974. The album was produced by Mentor Williams and featured guitarists Lonnie Mack and Troy Seals. However, the record was a commercial failure and Jans opted to relocate to Los Angeles.

After a period of isolation, Jans released a second album, The Eyes of An Only Child, on Columbia Records in 1975, executive produced by Lowell George. The album featured his song "Out of Hand", which later became a country hit for Gary Stewart. The song "Struggle in Darkness" was also a minor hit on FM radio, but the album was not a commercial success. His next album on Columbia Records, Dark Blonde (1976), also did not generate high sales, and Jans moved to Europe.

When the Columbia releases failed to find an audience, his career lost momentum and although Jans continued to perform, he issued no recordings until 1982's Champion, a Don Grusin-produced album that was released in Japan only.

Death and legacy 
Jans suffered serious injuries, especially to his kidneys, in a motorcycle accident in 1983. He died at age 36 of a suspected drug overdose in 1984. Mentor Williams's brother Paul sang "Loving Arms" at Jans's funeral.

Tom Waits dedicated a song to Jans, whom he and his wife had befriended, "Whistle Down the Wind (For Tom Jans)" from Bone Machine. Waits said of the song, "It was written about another friend, but it was the kind of song that Tom Jans would have written. He was there in spirit."

prompt: What is the physics behind the phenomenon of echolocation used by bats to navigate in the dark?
response:
Echolocation is a biological sonar system that allows certain animals, such as bats and some species of dolphins and whales, to navigate and locate prey in complete darkness or low-light environments. The physics behind this fascinating phenomenon involves the emission and reception of high-frequency sound waves.

Bats emit ultrasonic (high-frequency) calls, typically above 20 kHz, through their vocal cords or nasal passages. These calls travel through the air and bounce off objects in their environment, such as trees, buildings, and prey. When the sound wave encounters an object, it reflects back to the bat, known as an echo.

The bat's ears, which can be specialized structures like pinnae (external ear flaps) or auditory sacs (internal chambers), receive these echoes. By comparing the time delay between the emitted call and the received echo, the bat can calculate the distance to the object. This process is known as time difference of arrival (TDOA).

Moreover, by analyzing the frequency content of the echo, the bat can determine the size, shape, and texture of the object. This is because different surfaces reflect sound waves differently, resulting in unique echo patterns.

The physics behind echolocation also involve the principles of acoustics, including sound propagation, reflection, and diffraction. Bats can adjust the frequency and duration of their calls based on environmental factors, such as atmospheric conditions, to optimize their navigation and hunting abilities.

In summary, echolocation is a remarkable adaptation that enables bats to navigate and hunt effectively in low-light environments. It is a testament to the intricate interplay between biology and physics that has evolved over millions of years.

prompt: What is a mutt, and what are some of its characteristics?

A mutt, also known as a mixed breed dog, is a canine that is not purebred. This means that it is the result of two different breeds mating, producing offspring with a mix of genetic traits from both parents. Muts can vary widely in appearance, size, and temperament depending on the specific breeds involved in their ancestry. Some common characteristics of mutts include:

1. Unique appearance: Since they come from two or more different breeds, mutts often have a distinctive look that sets them apart from purebred dogs. Their coat color, pattern, and texture may be a combination of their parent breeds.

2. Versatile temperament: Because mutts inherit traits from multiple breeds, they can have a wide range of personalities. Some may be energetic and playful, while others may be calm and laid-back. Their temperament can depend on the breeds that make up their genetics.

3. However, any dog, regardless of breed, can develop health issues, so regular vet checkups are still important.

4. Adaptability: Mutts are often more adaptable to new environments and situations than purebred dogs because they have inherited a broader range of coping mechanisms from their parent breeds. They can be easier to train and socialize since they are not as set in their ways as purebred dogs.

5. Lower cost: Because mutts are not registered with a breed organization, they often cost less than purebred dogs due to lower registration fees and fewer breed-specific health tests required during breeding. Additionally, mutts are often available for adoption at shelters and rescue organizations, making them a more affordable option for those looking to add a furry friend to their family.

prompt: What is a sweatshop? What are some criticisms of the sweatshop labor model?
response:
A sweatshop, also known as a "sweat factory," is a type of workplace where workers are paid very low wages to produce goods under poor working conditions, often in dangerous and unhealthy environments. These factories are typically located in developing countries with weak labor laws and low wage standards. The term "sweatshop" comes from the fact that workers may be required to work long hours in hot and humid conditions, leading to excessive sweating.

Some criticisms of the sweatshop labor model include:

1. Poor Working Conditions: Sweatshops often have unsafe and unsanitary working conditions, such as inadequate ventilation, insufficient lighting, and lack of protective equipment. Workers may be exposed to hazardous chemicals, noise pollution, and other health risks.

2. Low Wages: Workers in sweatshops are often paid extremely low wages, which do not provide them with a living wage or sufficient income to support themselves and their families. In many cases, workers earn less than the local minimum wage or less than $2-3 per day.

3. Long Working Hours: Workers in sweatshops may be required to work extremely long hours, sometimes up to 16 hours a day or seven days a week, without overtime pay or breaks. This can lead to exhaustion, burnout, and physical and mental health issues.

4. Lack of Labor Rights: Many sweatshops operate in countries with weak labor laws or lack enforcement mechanisms, leaving workers vulnerable to exploitation and abuse. Workers may be denied basic labor rights, such as freedom of association, collective bargaining, and the right to form unions.

5. Child Labor: Some sweatshops employ child labor, which is prohibited by international labor standards. Children may be subjected to dangerous and exploitative working conditions, depriving them of education and childhood experiences.

These criticisms have led to calls for greater regulation and protection of worker rights in global supply chains. Companies and governments must ensure that workers are treated fairly and humanely, and that they receive a living wage and safe working conditions. Failure to address these issues can result in negative impacts on worker health, safety, and wellbeing, as well as reputational damage to brands and companies associated with sweatshops.

"We are testing this to see 'how does this impact our brand, how does this impact our infrastructure, our own stores and e-commerce, do we reach new segments ... and of course also what will the result look like'," he said in an interview.

To become more accessible, IKEA has in recent years invested heavily in expanding online and in new sales channels. It is now rolling out a new shoppable app as well as inner-city store formats.
